coverage_note: South Carolina has no public-sector collective bargaining statute in the sources captured (S.C. Code Title 8 chapters 11 and 17, Title 41 chapters 1 and 7 were searched). State payroll deduction of association dues is barred for any association that bargains collectively or encourages strikes, and the right-to-work chapter bars compulsory dues or fees.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. The right-to-work chapter makes it unlawful for an employer to require payment of any fees or dues as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: (A) It is unlawful for an employer to require an employee, as a condition of employment, or of continuance of employment to: (1) be or become or remain a member or affiliate of a labor organization or agency; (2) abstain or refrain from membership in a labor organization; or (3) pay any fees, dues, assessments, or other charges or sums of money to a person or organization.
